routes.label: Write both areas using the common perimeter

question: A circle and a square have the same perimeter. Then:
solution:
Let \(P>0\) be the common perimeter. Expressing both areas in terms of \(P\) lets us compare them directly.

The square has side length \(P/4\), so its area is
\[
A_{\text{square}}=\frac{P^2}{16}.
\]
The circle has radius \(P/(2\pi)\), so its area is
\[
A_{\text{circle}}=\pi\left(\frac{P}{2\pi}\right)^2
=\frac{P^2}{4\pi}.
\]
Because both areas are positive, we can compare their ratio:
\[
\frac{A_{\text{circle}}}{A_{\text{square}}}
=\frac4\pi>1,
\]
since \(\pi<4\). Therefore the circle has the greater area, choice B.
